name: SDK Runtime (privacy sandbox)
plain: Would have run ad SDKs in their own process so they could not read the host app's data.
meaning: Isolation of third-party SDKs from host app memory and identifiers. Never reached general availability; retired in the Oct 2025 announcement.

android.store_policy: Privacy Sandbox status page lists as scheduled for phaseout (page updated Aug 2026)
android.note: Google announced on 17 Oct 2025 it is retiring this along with most Privacy Sandbox APIs. No Android removal date was stated in the announcement.

limits.headline: Can't run ad tools in a separate box on Android, since Google retired it
limits.user_action: Nothing. It was a background feature that never reached wide release
can: Have kept ad tools away from the app's data (Android 14, never released widely)
Have limited what ad tools could see
Fall back to the plain model, where tools share the app's access
cannot: Run on iPhone; it is not an Apple feature
Count on it, since Google announced its retirement on 17 Oct 2025
limits.differs: Android only. iPhone never had it.

story.what_it_is: A plan to run ad code in its own sealed room so it cannot read the host app's data.

marketing.name: SDK Runtime
marketing.pitch: Android Privacy Sandbox plan to isolate ad SDKs from the app. Google retired it in October 2025.

story.for_you: You would not have noticed it. Ads would have loaded as before, but the ad code would have run in a separate process.
story.for_makers: It would have kept ad code from reading the app's memory and IDs. It never reached general availability and was retired in the October 2025 announcement.

use_cases.example: An ad SDK runs in a sealed process and cannot read the host app's user ID.
A game studio would have been able to add an ad network without fear it reads saves.
A news app would have stopped a rogue ad from scraping reading data.
Isolating code lowers the harm from a hacked SDK.
Analytics tools would have gotten only what the app handed them.
Developers tested the beta and found it hard to adapt popular SDKs.

story.android_note: Retired in October 2025 before reaching general availability.
story.ios_note: iOS has no equal. SDKs run inside the app's process.

technical_bounds: Retired: do not build new features on this
Ad ID stays the main cross-app identifier

legit_uses: Was meant as an ID-free ad system
